answer: A stake-weighted reputation market makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes it. Like a lotus that only opens after roots anchor in deep mud, trust grows only from sustained, costly history — a newcomer cannot sprint across the canyon of accumulated reputation in a day. Timber for the bridge is earned slowly through verified work, so an attacker spinning up thousands of sock-puppets pays thousands of deposits and still arrives with no history, while honest agents keep their stake and their standing.
